details.claim: The first Denisovan remains were found in Siberia's Denisova Cave.
Denisovans interbred with modern humans, with high levels of Denisovan DNA in Melanesians.
The Harbin cranium, identified as Denisovan in 2025, confirms their presence in China.

details.extra_statement: Denisovans, an extinct human species, roamed Siberia from 200,000 to 32,000 years ago.
Denisovans had dark skin and a distinct build.
Denisova Cave, in south-central Siberia, yielded the first Denisovan remains.
Other Denisovans were found in caves in China and Laos, expanding their known range.
No formal species name has been established, but they are closely related to Neanderthals.
